page: Microsoft Azure M8pds_v4 is an ARM-based, memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned via Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance is powered by an arm64 processor delivering 8 dedicated vCPUs paired with 128.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core allocation of 16.0 GB per vCPU. Graphics acceleration is absent with zero GPUs present. For high-speed scratch space, the server includes 472 GB of local NVMe SSD storage alongside support for external Premium Storage.

With a 1:16 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the configuration is structured to handle workloads prioritizing large memory pools over high core counts. Because it is built on the arm64 architecture, traditional x86 CPU instruction sets like AVX, AVX-512, and AMX are not available, requiring binaries compiled specifically for ARM64 environments. From a qualitative cost efficiency standpoint, the substantial memory density per core limits compute licensing overhead when deploying memory-bound services, while the bundled NVMe disk offers local high-speed I/O without requiring dedicated attached block devices. Zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provisioned by default.

This infrastructure profile fits memory-intensive applications including in-memory relational and key-value databases, distributed caching layers, real-time analytics engines, and memory-heavy ETL pipelines benefiting from fast local transient storage.
